Subject: Early traffic snapshot + pilot goals (SurgeonAI)

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the intro — we had a great demo with Marissa yesterday. SurgeonAI is ready to run a two-stage pilot: a low-latency inference endpoint for live surgical transcript summarization (Tier A) and a larger async batch job for nightly analytics (Tier B).

High-level asks for the pilot:
- Tier A: p99 latency target <= 200ms for short prompts (avg prompt 45 tokens, responses 60-120 tokens); initial concurrency target ~250 concurrent sessions with burst to 1k for 10–15 minutes around scheduled rounds.
- Tier B: nightly batch of ~15M tokens (mostly long-form responses ~800 tokens each), tolerant of 2–4 hour windows.

We want a rough capacity and cost plan before we commit to an NDA/PO. Can you share a suggested phased capacity playbook or a short questionnaire we can fill that captures prompt/response lengths, session duration, typical token mix, and acceptable fallbacks? I attached a small CSV with anonymized sample traces (prod_sample.csv) — you'll see the token histograms.

Best,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform @ SurgeonAI

Alex — thanks for the details and the sample. That helps a lot.

Quick ask: to size dedicated capacity predictably, we generally break pilots into two phases and ask for a short set of traffic details. I attached a small phased_capacity_template.csv that mirrors what our sizing engine needs. Can you fill the boxed fields and return? Key fields we need:
- typical prompt length distribution (p10/p50/p90)
- expected response length distribution for Tier A and Tier B
- session duration / idle timeout assumptions (are sessions persistent across multiple prompts?)
- per-request KV cache hit-rate (if you use session context caching)
- token-creation cadence (tokens/sec per session during bursts)

Notes on our side:
- For Tier A latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend reserving a small dedicated pool with autoscale headroom + a warm standby regional replica for failover.
- For Tier B we often recommend preemptible-backed batching nodes with higher throughput kernels.

Next step: once you return the template, Marissa will produce a two-stage capacity sketch (GPU mix, baseline reserved units, burst buffer, expected monthly token cost). If that looks good we can turn it into a mutual action plan and include Ben for pricing and commitment options.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex / Jamie — thanks for the quick turn on the template, very helpful. Draft plan and asks below; I kept this intentionally actionable so we can convert to a mutual action plan quickly.

Phase 1 (2–4 week pilot):
- Purpose: validate Tier A latency and session stickiness in the Western US region.
- Baseline reserved: equivalent of 6x A100-80GB (or mixed A100/GPU-gen equivalent) as a dedicated pool for inference with autoscale headroom to add up to 18x during bursts. This maps to our sizing assumptions with 250 sustained concurrent sessions and 1k burst.
- Caching/optimizations: enable prefix caching and session KV cache (we estimate 60% KV hit helps reduce GPU cycles by ~28%).
- Metrics to validate: p95/p99 latency, token cost per 1k prompts, KV cache hit, session rehydration latency.

Phase 2 (post-pilot, scale):
- Add batch nodes for Tier B (preemptible-friendly fleet) sized for 15M tokens over a 2 hour window — approx equivalent to 4-6 throughput workers depending on kernel selection.
- Fall-back: default to a smaller hosted variant for overflow routing if peak concurrency exceeds burst buffer to avoid queueing above p99 targets.

Risk & next steps:
- Risk: burst ramping faster than expected could cause transient queueing; we recommend a short chaos run during the pilot (one scheduled peak ramp) to validate autoscale + warm pool warmup times.
- Next step: Ben (cc'd) will prepare two commitment/pricing options (monthly reserved vs 12-month discount ladder) and a mutual action plan PDF. Marissa will produce an SLO checklist and sample runbook.

If that matches your expectations I’ll drop the MAP draft (one page) and a short MLE onboarding checklist by tomorrow afternoon. Would you like the pilot to include an early canary in us-west-2 only, or do you want multi-region from day one?
